newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Up despite low Taiwan award.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Up despite low Taiwan award.

text.p: Gasoline in Singapore moved up on Wednesday on aggressive bids by a Japanese trader despite a surprisingly low award into Taiwan's tender.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) will award its leaded 95-octane reformate tender on Thurdsay but awarded unleaded reformate for first-half May delivery at $27.40 per barrel cost-and-freight, a company official said.
The tender which closed April 1 and is valid for two days, required the two 250,000-barrel cargoes to be delivered to Keelung, Taichung, Kaohsiung or Shalung.
"We will award the leaded only tomorrow because the price is not so good," the official said.
The lowest offer for the leaded was around $28.40, c-and-f, traders said. CPC last bought a leaded cargo at $29.00 for April 1-15 delivery.

The unleaded cargo, said to be from a South Korean refiner, was made at a low level, compared to CPC's last tender, where it bought 250,000 barrels of unleaded reformate at a much higher $28.60 c-and-f, April 16-30 arrival.
"We received so many offers...14 when normally its around 10," a CPC source said.

The award was also lower than trades in Singapore with a Japanese trader actively bidding 95-octane unleaded cargoes and buying from a Singapore trader and a European major at $27.50 and $27.70 free-on-board Singapore lifting April 26-30 and 17-21, respectively.

The market was on the long side with prices in Singapore crashing by more than $1.00 per barrel on Monday to trade at $27.00. On Tuesday, prices recovered ahead of the close of Taiwan's tender with a bid from the the Japanese trader at $27.40.
But the Japanese buyer, who had already bought one million barrels in March and so far 150,000 barrels in April, said he was still in the market to buy.
